newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's FCL says lower prices to hit paper earnings.
newsitem.headline: NZ's FCL says lower prices to hit paper earnings.

text.p: Fletcher Challenge Ltd Chief Executive Hugh Fletcher said on Thursday that lower pulp and paper prices would result in "inadequate" earnings for the company's Paper Division.

Asked about half-year and full-year earnings prospects, Fletcher told reporters: "Clearly they are going to be inadequate, as a direct reflection of the marked decline in pulp and paper prices in the six months, in particular paper prices."
"This is an industry problem, severest in Asia and North America and less severe in Europe," Fletcher said.

Asked about the prospects of major players cutting back production, Fletcher said: "Some will and some have, and I think that will happen. The problem is that once prices bounce back up then people start resenting the loss of margin from that curtailment and they come back on stream," he said.
The pulp market had reached a delicate point in terms of downtime, he said.
FCL paper would take some downtime in its pulp and paper operations, as it had done in the first quarter and as it planned to do in the second quarter of its fiscal year to June.
The situation was being monitored week-by-week in each of its mills.
Fletcher said the other divisions were doing well, particularly FCL Energy, which was benefitting from high oil prices.
